parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
One of the mRNA codons for the amino acid Gln is CAA.
A mutation could change this codon from CAA to UAA.

UAA is a STOP codon.

State what is meant by a STOP codon.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Many proteins that contain the amino acids shown in Fig. 4.1 are globular.

Describe how the three R groups in Fig. 4.1 can contribute to the globular structure of a protein.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
An example of a globular protein is the enzyme starch phosphorylase. This enzyme catalyses the conversion of starch to glucose-1-phosphate.

Name the type of bond that is broken when starch is converted to glucose-1-phosphate.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem:
An investigation was carried out to find out how the activity of starch phosphorylase varied with temperature, when free in solution and when immobilised in alginate.

The results are shown in Fig. 4.2.
{{figure:figure_4_2.webp}}
Fig. 4.2
parts.text: With reference to Fig. 4.2, compare the results for the enzyme activity when free in solution and when immobilised.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: State how the Michaelis-Menten constant ($K_m$) is derived from $V_{max}$ for an enzyme.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem:
The $K_m$ values for starch phosphorylase were determined when free in solution and when immobilised.

The $K_m$ values were:

- free in solution, $K_m = 0.34\text{ mmol dm}^{-3}$
- immobilised, $K_m = 0.84\text{ mmol dm}^{-3}$.
parts.text: Suggest an explanation for the difference between the two values.
